Methods

Acoustic-ejection MS runs (2 plate(s), 384-well format, unit-resolution data, both mode) were analysed with TriADE 1.4.0. The interval between ejections was fitted to the total ion current (2.500 s) and each ejection was assigned to its well (row-serpentine (A1→A24, B24→B1, ...)). For each well the product ion(s) [M+H]+, [M+Na]+, [M-H]- were searched within ±0.5 Da of the calculated m/z in every spectrum from 0.45 s before to 0.6 s after the ejection apex. An ion was considered validated when the M peak was ≥ 200,000 cps with a distinct M+1 peak ≥ 50% of the cutoff in at least 2 spectra, and the ejection signal was ≥ 2× the median of the same m/z in the wells sharing the same reagent. Wells were graded in five confidence levels: 5 Present (evidence ≥ 1,000,000 cps), 4 Likely present (≥ 200,000 cps), 3 Check spectrum (≥ 80,000 cps, or a reagent ion on the product ion, carryover ≥ 5× from the previous ejection, or only a secondary adduct), 2 Likely absent (raw signal > 100,000 cps) and 1 Not detected; wells that could not be measured were sent to HPLC-MS. The standard detection criteria of the program were used. HPLC-MS conversion ≥ 5% defined the presence of the product; wells without an HPLC-MS result were counted as not detected.
